composition.note: Read the complete new profile and all relay_load_test.go changes. Read relevant exact production Relay and SDK owner/cancellation/stdio/HTTP paths, plus existing Windows memory observer. No source mutation or runtime by reviewer.

findings.condition: A canceled SDK CallTool retires its local outgoing request before the server response necessarily finishes the HTTP POST. Calling ClientSession.Close first closes IOTransport Reader before Writer.
findings.consequence: The fixture may close Relay stdout consumer before postWG drains a valid late cancellation response, causing io.ErrClosedPipe and a false regression failure or invalid drain evidence.
evidence: SDK mcp/transport.go call retires canceled calls; rwc.Close closes rc before wc.
SDK mcp/client.go ClientSession.Close delegates to connection.Close.
Production #629 HTTPToStdioRelay.Run waits postWG before canceling GET/terminating session.
findings.correction: Close only owned stdin first, keep SDK reader alive until Relay done; preserve bounded cancellation/pipe fallback, then close SDK session and output.

findings.location: echo cancellation branch and cancellation measurement
findings.condition: Old cancelFinished signal was sent before return and deferred active decrement.
findings.consequence: The old cancel_settlement_ns label could understate even the tool handler own cleanup and overclaim completed cancellation.
findings.correction: One deferred action decrements active before signaling canceled handler cleanup. Rename fields to cancelled_handler_cleanups_observed/cancel_handler_cleanup_ns. Full HTTP/Relay/SDK-session settlement is checked separately after close.

source_checks.scope: Test-only profile plus fixture InitializeResult protocolVersion compatibility. No production Relay implementation, dependency, retry contract or new framework is changed.
source_checks.response_oracle: Every successful CallTool checks exact worker/iteration sequence and full payload, content count/type and IsError. Worker failures prevent reporting completed/lost counts. Server exact total covers warmup+held+measured+cancel calls; held barrier establishes exact max-active worker count.
source_checks.workload: Three finite closed-loop cases: 1x1x64 at 1 KiB, 8x1x32 at 1 KiB, 4x4x16 at 64 KiB; at most 16 tools simultaneously. Each case uses its own loopback server, transport, pipes and a 45 s context.
source_checks.synchronization: Latency slots are disjoint per worker and read only after all result channel receives. Sampler state is read only after samplesDone. Atomics protect server/HTTP counts; no observed shared-buffer/data race in the proposed schedule.
source_checks.lifecycle: Owned input interruption capability is explicit. Reordered close keeps reader alive through accepted response drain. Server counters and Sessions() are checked after explicit peer/HTTP close. Cleanup callbacks are idempotent on normal path; failed timeout is not treated as settled.
source_checks.measurement: Whole process memory is declared. Windows resident total/private and private commit are separate. Independent field maxima are sampled lower bounds, with availability false when samples==0. Allocation counters are differences across measured interval; all driver/sampler costs remain included.
source_checks.cancellation: Client cancellation and handler own cleanup are checked separately. New name intentionally does not claim entire internal SDK response completed at handler signal time.
source_checks.load_fixture_diff: InitializeResult gains protocolVersion, initialized response oracle requires it, and EOF-drain fixture emits a matching valid version result. This preserves its session admission when composed with current #629.
source_checks.local_syntax_check: git diff --check PASS only; no Go parser/build/test/gofmt executed by reviewer.

remaining_limits: No runtime, compiler, formatter, race-detector or actual performance result is established by this review. Exact final formatted inputs still need binding and qualified execution.
The profile exercises real SDK transport/dispatch with synthetic tools. It is not installed Hub, external consumer service or a production service-level objective.

Process measurements include SDK client/server, Relay, driver/sampler, payload, latency arrays and deliberately reachable cleanup closures/closed objects. Retained-after-close values do not by themselves prove a Relay leak or the memory of a standalone Relay executable.
Nominal 5 ms samples can miss transients; per-field maxima need not occur simultaneously. If sampled_peak_available=false there are no workload-time samples, only the baseline seed.

GET request count is observed but no pre-baseline GET barrier, server-initiated GET message workload or forced reconnect exists in this profile. Prior #629 32/32 GET reconnect evidence remains separate. POST-origin resumption remains outside the implementation/profile.
Call integrity is at SDK call/result level, not a byte-level oracle for every duplicate wire frame silently retired or discarded by SDK.

Internal jsonrpc2 connection.go was not available in the locally supplied reference set. Public Close code, IOTransport, SDK call retirement and HTTP session-close paths were inspected; internal connection scheduling was not reconstructed by assumption.

Two Relay close waits fail explicitly on deadline; a failed run does not prove an unresponsive inner lifetime settled. Root runner must enforce admitted process ownership/time/output limits and retain actual nested results.
